segments.text: The Inner Lock lay behind the Long Quay, where the old wet dock opened into the basin. It was a granite trench sixty paces long and twelve wide, with a pair of black timber gates at each end. The gates at the head held back the wet dock, which was full and flat and green and smelled of weed. The gates at the tail held back the basin, which was falling. Between them the chamber was empty. Its floor was wet stone, with weed in the cracks and a long puddle down the middle where the last of the water had not drained, and a man in a waistcoat was walking along it with a lantern, kicking at things.
